paper.title: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
paper.central_claim: A GPT-4o 'LLM-as-Judge' that scores 10 sampled UI-TARS-2B responses per AGUVIS instance yields preference pairs for DPO that make a lightweight, privacy-preserving, locally-run 2B GUI agent outperform its baseline on OSWorld without human annotation.
paper.claim_scope: Single-step AGUVIS instances, UI-TARS-2B only, OSWorld 369 tasks at 15 and 50 steps; privacy/local-efficiency claims are framing, not tested.

evidence.quote: we introduce an LLM-as-Judge framework that automatically evaluates and filters synthetic interaction trajectories, producing high-quality data for reinforcement learning without human annotation
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated method and its data claim (trajectories, human-free).

evidence.quote: developing a lightweight vision-language model that runs entirely on local machines
evidence.support_explanation: Privacy / local-deployment framing of the central claim.

evidence.quote: how to obtain high-quality GUI interaction data without extensive human labeling
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated problem.

evidence.quote: we first sampled multiple responses from our base policy model, UI-TARS-2B, using task instances from the AGUVIS dataset
evidence.support_explanation: Candidates come from the policy being trained, on AGUVIS task instances.

evidence.quote: with the goal of predicting the next interaction step within the graphical interface
evidence.support_explanation: AGUVIS instances are single-step next-action prediction, not trajectories.

evidence.quote: we generate a set of 10 diverse candidate completions
evidence.support_explanation: k=10 samples per instance.

evidence.quote: we present GPT-4o with 10 sampled responses from UI-TARS-2B alongside the ground truth answer, all within a single prompt.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge input = sampled responses + ground-truth answer (the judge has the label); no screenshot is mentioned for the judge.

evidence.quote: We instruct GPT-4o to assign a quality score between 0 and 100 to each response based on its relevance, accuracy, and alignment with the task instruction.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge output: 0-100 score per response.

evidence.quote: The first strategy pairs each model-generated response with a score below 80 against the corresponding ground-truth answer.
evidence.support_explanation: Pair type 1: ground truth chosen vs low-scored model sample rejected (threshold 80).

evidence.quote: The second strategy constructs preference pairs directly between model-generated responses.
evidence.support_explanation: Pair type 2: judge-ordered model-vs-model pairs.

evidence.quote: with the vast majority of samples receiving a score of 0 and only a small fraction scoring between 5 and 50.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge scores are almost all 0, so most pairs reduce to wrong-vs-gold; little graded signal.
15-step OSWorld weighted success: DPO-1/2/3 vs baseline 6.91.
Relative improvements at 15 steps.
50-step OSWorld weighted success; baseline 8.83.
At 50 steps gains are ~0 and DPO-3 regresses.

evidence.quote: for each models, we run the evaluation three times and average the performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Three runs averaged; spread not reported.

evidence.quote: our system did experience hardware failures during inference in some 50-step runs, which could have contributed to degraded performance.
evidence.support_explanation: 50-step measurements are partially corrupted by infrastructure failures (no rerun).

evidence.quote: all DPO models perform worse under the 50-step setting compared to their 15-step counterparts.
evidence.support_explanation: More steps lowers DPO models; baseline improves 6.91 -> 8.83.

evidence.quote: DPO models in the 15-step setting still outperform the baseline even when it operates under the more flexible 50-step setting.
evidence.support_explanation: Claim of efficiency at shorter budgets (9.33 vs 8.83 is 0.5 points).

evidence.quote: Overall, DPO-3 demonstrates the most consistent and robust gains, validating the benefit of integrating both preference supervision schemes.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim about DPO-3 consistency; contradicted by Table 2.

evidence.quote: By leveraging GPT-4 to automatically evaluate model-generated interaction trajectories, we construct high-quality preference pairs for Direct Preference Optimization.
evidence.support_explanation: Conclusion again says trajectories (and GPT-4 vs GPT-4o), but the pipeline is single-step (E005).

evidence.quote: we conduct a qualitative analysis of failure cases by manually inspecting samples where the agent failed to complete the task.
evidence.support_explanation: Failure analysis is qualitative, with no counts.
Per-domain cells are noisy (VLC baseline 1.96 vs DPO-1 16.50), reflecting a few tasks per domain.

evidence.quote: Max Diff is computed based on the best performance compared to the average baseline
evidence.support_explanation: Max-Diff column compares the best DPO variant to the baseline mean, an optimistic statistic.

evidence.quote: Our environment consists of five dedicated servers, each with dual Intel ® Xeon ® Platinum 8468 Processors, 1TB of RAM
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation ran on cloud servers with hosted vLLM endpoints, not on consumer/local hardware.
No human validation of the GPT-4o judge, no judge-vs-rule or judge-vs-exact-match comparison, and no ablation of any pipeline component appears anywhere in the paper.
No DPO hyper-parameters (beta, learning rate, epochs, batch size, adapters) and no number of preference pairs or training samples are reported.
No SFT-on-ground-truth baseline (same samples, same backbone) is reported, so DPO with judge scores is not separated from plain training on the labels.
No latency, memory, on-device or privacy measurement is reported even though the central framing is a privacy-preserving, resource-efficient local agent.

evidence.quote: UI-TARS [ 13 ] introduces a self-reflective task-aware decision-making framework that employs DPO to refine action selection through recursive evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors position UI-TARS DPO as the closest prior work.

evidence.quote: where annotators pinpoint mistakes in agent-generated traces and label the corrective actions
evidence.support_explanation: UI-TARS builds DPO pairs from human-annotated corrections; this paper swaps annotators for a GPT-4o scorer that already sees the gold action.

evidence.quote: A separate VLM evaluator assesses trajectory quality to ensure effectiveness.
evidence.support_explanation: VLM-as-evaluator for GUI data filtering already exists (AgentTrek) and was human-validated there (1,081 trajectories reviewed); this paper reports no validation.

evidence.quote: which comprises 369 real-world computer tasks involving web and desktop applications in open domains
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation set size: 369 OSWorld tasks.

evidence.quote: Each agent has maximum 15 steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Step budget definition for the headline table.

signatures.object: UI-TARS-2B policy weights via offline DPO on judge-built preference pairs
signatures.information: GPT-4o sees the instruction text (task, action space, output format), 10 sampled responses and the ground-truth answer; screenshot access for the judge is not described.
signatures.operation: Sample 10 responses/instance from the policy; GPT-4o scores each 0-100; build pairs either (gold chosen, model response <80 rejected) or (higher-scored vs lower-scored model responses); DPO.
signatures.output: DPO-1 (gold vs low), DPO-2 (model vs model), DPO-3 (union).
signatures.conditions: Labeled single-step data (gold answers) must exist; the policy must make many low-score responses.
signatures.feedback: Judge score relative to the gold answer; no environment feedback.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Threshold 80 for rejection; model-vs-model pairs need different scores; most scores are 0 (E011); no validation of the judge.
signatures.later_use: OSWorld evaluation with 15 and 50 steps, 3 runs averaged
signatures.claimed_effect: Weighted success 6.91 -> 9.33 (+35%) at 15 steps (E012, E013); ~0 at 50 steps (E014, E015).
signatures.failure_boundary: No 50-step gain; DPO-3 -6.68% at 50 steps (E015); invalid/wrong coordinates and repeated wrong actions remain (E022).

gap.author_gap: Cloud-hosted VLM agents raise privacy/cost concerns; a compact local agent is hard to train without costly human labeling (E002, E003).
gap.checked_gap: The labels already exist: the judge is given the AGUVIS gold answer (E007), so the claimed 'no human annotation' problem is not what the judge solves; its role reduces to graded matching of a sampled action to the label. The local/privacy problem is a deployment framing that the method (DPO fine-tuning) does not address and the paper does not measure (E025, E029). Nearest neighbors: UI-TARS DPO with human-annotated corrections (E031), AgentTrek VLM evaluator with human validation (E032).

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: DPO from corrected-vs-erroneous action pairs with human annotators; no ablation isolating reflection tuning in UI-TARS per domain card K26
VLM evaluator filters synthesized trajectories and was validated against human labels
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: not applied to DPO pair building

gap.residue: Whether a GPT-4o scorer adds anything over exact/semantic matching to the gold action when the gold action is in its prompt; whether the gain survives an SFT baseline on the same data; any measurable local-efficiency benefit.
gap.stakes: Cheap preference data for small GUI policies; but the delta from UI-TARS is a label-source swap (human annotator -> GPT-4o with gold).
gap.method_response: Replace annotators by an LLM scorer and pair the gold with sampled errors; evaluate online.
gap.remaining_gap: No judge reliability, no SFT/rule-reward control, 50-step null, no local-efficiency evidence, trajectories vs single-step mismatch.
gap.unresolved: Whether any part of the 15-step gain is attributable to the judge rather than to training on gold labels.

claims.text: DPO models outperform the UI-TARS-2B baseline on OSWorld under a 15-step budget (weighted success 6.91 -> 9.33, +35%).
claims.selection_vs_test: DPO-1/2/3 all evaluated and reported on the same test set; no dev split
claims.result_denominator: 3.14-point max difference; per-domain cells based on few tasks (E023)
claims.allowed_conclusion: A modest (about 2.4 point) average gain over the base model at 15 steps; not attributed to the judge.

claims.text: DPO also helps at 50 steps / shorter budgets are more efficient.
claims.allowed_conclusion: No reliable gain at 50 steps; the 15-step vs 50-step baseline comparison differs by 0.5 points.

claims.text: The LLM-as-Judge produces high-quality preference data without human annotation.
claims.setting: GPT-4o with gold answer in prompt
claims.allowed_conclusion: Judge quality is unmeasured; the gold answer is itself human labeled data.

claims.text: The resulting agent is privacy-preserving and resource-efficient on local machines.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Only that a 2B model can be fine-tuned; no local deployment evidence.

claims.text: DPO-3 (combined pairs) is the most consistent and robust.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Offline DPO of UI-TARS-2B on GPT-4o-scored pairs from AGUVIS single-step instances raises 3-run-averaged OSWorld success from 6.91 to 9.33 under a 15-step cap; no gain is shown at 50 steps, and neither the judge nor the privacy/local claims are supported.
unresolved: judge validity and necessity vs gold-label matching/SFT
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; nothing was re-run.
assessment.evidence_level_note: 'online' (not transfer): OSWorld is the only benchmark, was not a training source, but is also the sole reporting/selection target among DPO-1/2/3 and no second platform is tested.

G.reason: Two framings (no-human-label data; privacy-preserving local agent) but the gold labels already exist in the judge prompt, local deployment is neither diagnosed nor measured, and the closest prior (UI-TARS DPO, AgentTrek evaluator) is only named, not compared.

M.reason: Concrete pair construction (gold vs low-scored sample, model-vs-model) is a reasonable DPO recipe, but the judge's marginal role over label matching is not argued, scores collapse near 0 (E011), and the single-step data does not match the 'trajectory' framing.

X.reason: Sampling parameters, threshold 80 and two pairing rules are given; DPO settings, data size, judge prompt text and observation setting are missing, and failure boundaries are limited to a qualitative 3-way failure listing.

E.measurement.reason: Online execution-checked OSWorld success, 3-run average, but small absolute values (6.9-9.3%), noisy per-domain cells, 50-step arm damaged by hardware failures, and the training-time judge has no human validation.

E.causality.reason: Only DPO-1/2/3 vs the base model; no SFT-on-gold, rule-reward, judge-free, or pair-size controls, so the gain cannot be attributed to the judge or to preference structure.

E.holdout.reason: OSWorld is not an AGUVIS source, which is a reasonable holdout, but no overlap check, one benchmark only, and DPO variants are selected/reported on the same test tasks.

E.statistics.reason: Three runs but no spread; margins of 2-3 points on 369 tasks; per-domain cells based on a few tasks; the best-variant 'Max Diff' statistic is optimistic; 50-step results mixed and partly invalidated.

E.cost.reason: Same inference parameters and step caps for baseline and DPO models, and evaluation throughput is reported, but data-generation cost (GPT-4o calls), training compute, and on-device latency/memory are absent despite the resource-efficiency framing.

status.reason: Full html text read (short paper, no appendix); judge prompt and figures are images and not available in text, which does not block scoring because the pipeline and tables are described in prose.

rationale.summary: A short workshop-style paper: GPT-4o (given the gold answer) scores 10 sampled UI-TARS-2B responses per AGUVIS instance; pairs of gold-vs-low-score or high-vs-low model responses train DPO variants. At 15 steps OSWorld weighted success rises from 6.91 to 9.33; at 50 steps the gains vanish. The headline framing (human-free trajectory data, privacy-preserving local agent) is not matched by operations or measurements.
strengths: Online execution-based evaluation on OSWorld with three averaged runs
Honest reporting of the 50-step null and hardware failures
weaknesses: Judge is never validated and sees the gold answer, so its necessity is unshown
No SFT, rule-reward or judge ablation; no DPO hyper-parameters or data size
